sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Industrial Quick-Freezing of Steamed Dim Sum and Dumplings

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic heritage harmonized with EU company law and AML/CFT directives)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: China-Luxembourg Double Taxation Agreement and protocol, as amended by the OECD Multilateral Instrument
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network
EU Treaty rights of establishment, free movement of capital and related dispute-resolution mechanisms

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; Law of 12 November 2004 on the Fight against Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 26 February 2019; CSSF and Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU Luxembourg) implementing standards for obliged entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each proposed shareholder and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority; notarized by a qualified notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the country of origin is an Apostille Convention member; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with certified French translation if originally issued in a non-Luxembourg official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution authorizing incorporation in Luxembourg and appointing the local incorporator or manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or supervisory board of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in the country of origin, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and source-of-funds statement for each individual holding 25% or more
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary preparing the incorporation deed, with supporting KYC collected from the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille/consular legalization where the declaration is executed abroad; signature before the Luxembourg notary accepted for domestic execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every shareholder, director, manager, authorized signatory and 25% or more UBO against Luxembourg FIU sanctions circular, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, and credible adverse-media/integrity sources. PEP status is assessed at formation, prior to bank account opening, and on an ongoing risk-based basis. Negligent failure to detect a sanctioned PEP triggers liability under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF enforcement rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) portal: https://www.lbr.lu / https://www.rcs.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be submitted in Latin script and is registered in French administrative usage. Non-Latin script names require official transliteration and certified French or German transcription. The legal form suffix must appear as 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée', 'SARL', or 'S.à r.l.' The RCS will reject a name that is identical or confusingly similar to an existing legal entity name, registered trademark, official emblem, or name protected under Luxembourg public policy.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 calendar days of receiving an RCS refusal notice, the applicant may file a written request for reconsideration through a Luxembourg-registered lawyer, attaching the proposed articles of association, name-search output, and a memorandum explaining distinctive elements. If the refusal is confirmed, the applicant may lodge a judicial appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber), with notice to the RCS and, where relevant, the Ministry of Justice. All appeal documents must be in French and signed by an avocat admitted in Luxembourg.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is acceptable for the administrative registered office of an SARL, but it is not acceptable for the industrial factory footprint of an ISIC 1074 frozen-food production unit. The food-processing establishment requires a licensed physical facility in Luxembourg with appropriate hygiene, production, cold-chain storage and personnel areas before the operating authorization can issue. The registered office may share administrative functions with a service provider, but a production licence may never be based solely on a virtual office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High quantified risk: approximately 65-75% probability of an unannounced food-safety and hygiene inspection within the first 12 months of production. Additional unannounced inspections by the labor inspectorate, customs, and environmental authorities are reasonably foreseeable, given the industrial food-processing scope.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Online name search and conditional name reservation
Notarial drafting and execution of SARL incorporation deed
RCS registration and publication in the Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
Application for commercial establishment license (autorisation d'établissement)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economy / Direction générale des classes moyennes

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Food factory establishment license and hygiene registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Food Safety Authority (ALVA) / Ministry of Health
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory food-business registration and inspection tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
PEP, OFAC, EU, UN and Luxembourg sanctions screening for proposed shareholders and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML/KYC screening provider engaged by the Luxembourg law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate per screened individual and corporate parent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French or German translation of foreign corporate, passport and apostilled documents
Hague Apostille and consular legalization fees in jurisdiction of origin of foreign shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / designated apostille authority in country of origin, plus Luxembourg consular post
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official legalization and apostille tariffs, plus courier expenses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg law firm incorporation coordination, appointment of manager, and UBO/KYC file assembly
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing hourly rate fixed-fee arrangement for Standard SARL incorporation with licensed food factory scope

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office service for first year of the SARL (administrative seat service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing annual market fee for a licensed corporate registered-office provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 180 to 203-1 (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and Accounting; amended Law of 2 September 2011 on Business Establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Electronic Desk (e-Desk)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation with Articles of Association (Acte constitutif avec statuts), registered with the RCS and published in the electronic compendium RESA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid up at constitution. Since the 2016 reform, no mandatory escrow blocking account is required; the notary must certify that subscription funds are effectively paid and freely available at the company's disposal on signature of the deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE [NAME] SARL (unanimous): (1) The statutory share capital is subscribed in full at EUR 12,000, allocated to the subscribers as set out in the notarized deed; the capital has been duly paid up and certified available to the company by the notary. (2) The registered office is hereby adopted and fixed at [address], Luxembourg. (3) [Name] is appointed authorized manager (gérant) with full powers to administer and represent the company. (4) The gérant is directed to complete RCS registration, tax registrations, and the environmental and food-safety permits, and to ensure all statutory filings are made. Adopted this [date] at Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name pre-validation and KYC dossier assembly
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) name index; Luxembourg notary advisory (LuxNotary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an official search in the RCS index to confirm name availability and reject similar protected names; instruct the notary to draft the articles of association; collect certified identification, criminal records, proof of address and UBO information for all subscribers and proposed gérants.
required_dossiers: Certified passport/ID copies of subscribers and managers
Recent criminal record certificates (country of residence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or collides with an existing registration, immediately re-file a revised name check with a distinct corporate name and update the draft articles before notarization; the name refusal itself is not appealable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the incorporation bank account and capital subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg-licensed credit institution (or registered branch) acting for the SARL en formation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a bank account in the name of the future SARL 'en formation'; each subscriber transfers its part of the EUR 12,000 minimum capital; obtain a bank certificate confirming payment and the immediate availability of funds for the notary's verification.
required_dossiers: Bank account application for SARL en formation
Business plan for frozen dim sum and dumpling production
KYC and customer due diligence documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening, subscription funds may be held in a notarial sequestration account until execution of the deed, and an alternative bank may be selected; the notary documents the substitute arrangement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarized deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with all subscribers (or holders of notarial proxies); the notary reads the articles, verifies lawful objects, certifies full payment of the share capital, records any in-kind contribution valuation, and obtains signatures to finalize the acte constitutif.
required_dossiers: Final articles of association signed by all shareholders
Bank certificate or sequestration certificate evidencing paid-up capital
Identity documents of subscribers and proposed gérant(s)
Notarial powers of attorney, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any irregularity flagged by the notary is corrected before signature; post-signature errors are cured by a supplementary notarial rectification deed, followed by a supplementary RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS Electronic Desk (e-Desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or legal counsel e-files the notarized deed, notarial conformity certificate and registration request through the LBR e-Desk; pay the RCS duty (approx. EUR 19); the RCS verifies legal conformity within five working days and issues the RCS registration extract; the corporate notice is then published in the RESA electronic compendium.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of RCS duties
Request for insertion in the RCS register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, the filer must respond within the granted deadline (usually 15 days) by completing or correcting the filing through e-Desk; if the registration is refused, a corrected dossier may be re-submitted and the refusal decision may be appealed before the Luxembourg administrative courts within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation administrative opening: VAT, business establishment permit and social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Ministry of Economy via MyGuichet; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the RCS extract: (a) register for VAT through MyGuichet; (b) file the autorisation d'établissement application identifying the frozen-food manufacturing activity; (c) register with the CCSS as employer; (d) submit the initial food establishment approval notification to ALVA, including the HACCP-linked plan required by Regulation (EC) No 852/2004.
required_dossiers: Professional qualification certificates of managers (food technology or equivalent)
Manager identity documents and criminal records
HACCP summary and food safety plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry of Economy or ALVA requests missing information, upload the supplementary documents through MyGuichet within the stated period; if the authorization is refused, seek administrative recourse before the administrative courts within three months and, where appropriate, re-apply with a corrected file.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - General Directorate for SMEs and Entrepreneurship (Direction générale des PME et de l'entreprenariat)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for industrial food manufacturing, combined with the environmental operating permit (autorisation d'exploitation) for classified establishments under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 and food establishment approval under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 1 classified establishment (industrial food processing) requiring a prior integrated environmental operating permit; an EIA screening is required depending on installed freezing capacity and annual production tonnage, with a possible full EIA report for installations exceeding the screening thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 May 2014 on waste water discharges: pH 6-9; BOD5 less than or equal to 25 mg/L; COD less than or equal to 125 mg/L; total suspended solids less than or equal to 35 mg/L; total nitrogen less than or equal to 15 mg/L; total phosphorus less than or equal to 2 mg/L. Air and odour: conformity with the BAT conclusions of the BREF for Food, Drink and Milk Industries, with odour concentration not exceeding 300 ouE/m3 at the property boundary; waste cooking oil and food waste handling per the waste hierarchy obligations; ammonia refrigeration risk assessment if applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and commissioning certificate from the Administration des services de secours (CGDIS) under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 September 2008; structural load certification of the industrial building and cold-store envelope by an approved engineer; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering freezer emergency alarms, cold-store exit locks, forklift traffic, ammonia refrigeration safety and first-aid provisions.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT. Electronic portals: MyGuichet (myguichet.lu) and guichet.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign founder must first incorporate a SARL before a Luxembourg notary and file the articles of association with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), obtaining a 13-digit RCS registration number which constitutes the national business/matricule number. The RCS number is then used as the TIN for direct tax purposes without separate registration, but the company must file a corporate taxpayer profile with the ACD. For VAT, the SARL must submit Form 640 (VAT registration application) to the AEDT before starting taxable activities, accompanied by the RCS extract, identity documents of directors/partners, evidence of business premises, and a description of intended supplies. Non-resident entities without a fixed establishment must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative unless using the OSS/IOSS scheme; the AEDT then issues a Luxembourg VAT number beginning with 'LU' followed by eight characters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no U.S.-style check-the-box or pass-through election for SARLs; SARLs are transparently not considered. Statutory elections available include: election for fiscal unity (integration fiscale) for corporate income tax and municipal business tax among at least 95% owned resident group companies; option to form a VAT group; election to apply the special IP (patent and IP box) regime for qualifying intangible income; irrevocable election for the notional interest deduction; and option for the simplified VAT flat-rateâreimbursement in certain sectors.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 30,000 annual taxable turnover for the small undertaking exemption; VAT registration becomes mandatory above this threshold. Non-resident taxable persons supplying goods or services in Luxembourg are required to register from the first euro unless the supply is covered by OSS/IOSS or is a B2B service where the reverse charge applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls (CTC), no API-based invoice stamping, and no digital mark or QR code mandate for B2B/B2C invoices. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only for B2G invoices to public authorities, which must be submitted electronically via the PEPPOL network through the Invoice.lu platform. All VAT invoices must follow EU invoicing rules, and copies must be retained for at least six (or, in practice, ten) years for audit purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods physically exported to a destination outside the European Union qualify for the 0% VAT rate provided (i) the goods are dispatched or transported by the supplier or a third party acting on behalf of the customer; (ii) export occurs within the legal time limits (normally goods must leave the EU within 90 days of the supply date or the discretionary longer period must be documented); (iii) the supplier obtains and retains documentary proof of export, including customs exit confirmation; and (iv) the invoice clearly states that the supply is an export subject to zero-rating. Offshore services, ancillary transport, loading, warehousing, and processing services directly related to exported goods may also be zero-rated, or are outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT where the place of supply is located outside Luxembourg under B2B place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/DAU) with exit stamp or electronic PLDA export confirmation
Bill of Lading (B/L) or other transport document (CMR waybill, AWB, rail consignment note)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank SWIFT confirmation of payment for the exported goods
Export/sanitary certificate for food products (including EU health and phytosanitary certificates for buns/dim sum)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may subject zero-rating claims to documentary audit and may retrospectively claw back VAT at the standard 17% rate plus default interest if the exporter cannot demonstrate physical export within the statutory period or if documentation is incomplete, false, or fraudulent. Penalties under Luxembourg VAT law include administrative fines up to EUR 2,500, a recovery surcharge of 10-20% of the tax due, and late-payment interest running from the original due date. Intentional VAT evasion or the deliberate use of fake customs declarations constitutes criminal tax fraud, punishable on conviction by imprisonment of up to five years and/or penal tax fines, and extends the reassessment limitation period from five to ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), in conjunction with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as banking and AML supervisory authority; foreign exchange controls are abolished under EU free movement of capital rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full convertibility of both current and capital account transactions for EUR and all freely convertible currencies. No prior administrative authorisation is required for payment of imports, repatriation of proceeds, dividends, interest, loan repayments or liquidation distributions to non-resident shareholders, subject to corporate law formalities and tax compliance. Profit remittance requires audited statutory accounts, a board decision proposing distribution, a general meeting resolution declaring the dividend, and compliance with Luxembourg dividend withholding tax and any relevant tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may freely retain proceeds in foreign currency accounts, convert at commercial bank rates, or net them against import obligations. All such transactions must merely be reported by the local bank for BCL balance-of-payments statistical purposes pursuant to the BCL external transactions reporting framework.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) – Spuerkeess
Société Générale Bank & Trust Luxembourg S.A.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low as a sole or primary banking relationship. Luxembourg law, via the amended Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the PSD2 implementing Law of 8 June 2017, permits electronic money institutions (EMIs) licensed by the CSSF or a passporting EU authority to provide payment accounts; however, a Luxembourg SARL's subscription capital must be paid into a bank account, and standard banking KYC/reference requirements under domestic AML law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended) do not afford EMIs the same unsecured credit depth as Tier-1 banks. Offshore digital EMIs without an EU passport are not legally viable as an account provider for a Luxembourg holding/operating entity and will be rejected by auditors and counterparties. An EU-licensed EMI may serve only as a supplementary settlement sub-channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg credit institutions generally permit remote onboarding using secure video-identification if the director/UBO is an EU resident and beneficial-ownership documentation is clear. However, leading banks (BIL, BGL, BCEE) frequently require at least one physical meeting in Luxembourg for the managing director and ultimate beneficial owner, or a personal visit by a bank due-diligence officer, especially when the parent chain contains non-EU entities. For a frozen-food manufacturing subsidiary, anticipate an in-person board meeting and notarised certificate of incorporation before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or non-transparent ultimate beneficial ownership chain involving cross-border holding entities or nominee shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete written shareholder structure ending at natural persons; notarised statutory documents (articles of association, deed of incorporation, shareholders ledger) for the SARL and each intermediate holding; certificates of good standing, register of directors and shareholders, and corporate tax residency certificates for all significant chain entities; a written UBO explanation with supporting identities and passport copies; a group company organigram signed by the statutory auditor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions or counterparties connected to high-risk jurisdictions, sanctions-listed persons, or unusual trade invoice patterns for food raw materials.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply full commercial invoice and packing list set, freight/customs declarations (EAD/ENS), import/export licences relevant to ISIC 1074 production, board-approved purchase/off-take agreements, counterparty AML/KYC due diligence reports, sanctions screening output from reputable screening tool, and a profit-margin explanation for the frozen dim-sum/dumpling manufacturing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injected share capital from a non-banking or third-country parent without clear commercial substance or previous banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide source-of-funds evidence from the parent's bank account statements and subscription ledger; notarised board resolution on capital increase; share subscription receipts; a capitalisation table for the SARL; valuation of any in-kind contributions (e.g. production machinery, intellectual property, prepaid leases) by an independent auditor; corporate tax and substance documentation (physical premises, payroll, fixed assets, operational licences, ISIC 1074 food-safety permits).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For cash capital subscriptions: transfer via SWIFT MT103 from the parent shareholder's bank to the Luxembourg SARL's blocked capital-escrow account at BIL, BCEE or BGL BNP Paribas, quoting the purpose 'Share capital / capital contribution under Act of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies'. Remittance must include the BCL balance-of-payments statistical transaction code corresponding to foreign direct investment equity; the notary's certificate and the deed of incorporation must be presented to the receiving bank. No foreign-exchange approval is required. For loans or shareholder advances, use SWIFT MT103/202 and the correct external-loan/interest code; attach a board resolution authorising the loan, a written shareholder-loan agreement, and confirmation that the interest and principal will be serviced through a lawful Luxembourg bank account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EU-zone trade settlements use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) in EUR. Non-EU suppliers and documentary transactions use SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic wire), optionally supported by an Irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT707. The LC is routed through the Luxembourg issuing bank (BIL, BCEE, BGL BNP Paribas) and advised by the seller's confirming/correspondent bank; payment is released against fully compliant documents (invoice, bill of lading/CMR, sanitary certificates, inspection reports, origin certificates). For repeated frozen-dough or packaging imports, consider an import open-account facility or bank guarantee; for exports to EU retail chains, use SEPA Direct Debit or supply-chain finance rails subject to the bank's commercial-lending approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forward (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CNH) with a documented underlying export/import exposure
FX Swap (rollover/spread for short-term treasury needs) executed under ISDA/EFET documentation
Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) for non-convertible or restricted pegged currencies where physical delivery is legally unavailable
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swap (CCIRS) to hedge operational debt denominated in USD or CNY against the EUR functional currency
European Vanilla FX Options (buy-side) to secure a maximum conversion cost without upfront premium, subject to bank credit line and board treasury mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (Comptes Annuels) filed under GAAP
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 7 months after financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end); shareholder approval required within 6 months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subject to administrative fine up to €2,000; persistent non-filing can trigger a formal notice and judicial strike-off from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers; automatic extension to 30 November when filed electronically; non-calendar year-ends due within 5 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid corporate income tax; late-filing fine up to €7,500; criminal penalties for intentional omission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May for calendar-year taxpayers; automatic extension to 30 November when filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delinquency interest of 0.6% per month; administrative fine up to €7,500; tax officer may issue ex-officio assessment for non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE, part of LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late confirmation subject to administrative penalty up to €1,250; repeated or serious violations may result in criminal fines up to €50,000 and imprisonment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if exceeding at least two of the three thresholds at balance sheet date: total balance sheet > €4,400,000; net turnover > €8,800,000; average number of employees > 50. Also mandatory for public-interest entities and any company forming part of a consolidated group exceeding the same thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Commercial Code (articles 28 et seq., implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is optional for unlisted companies and mandatory for listed entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE register must be confirmed annually and exclusively via the online RBE portal before 31 December. The confirmation validates the existing beneficial ownership data. Any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership arising during the year must be filed within 21 days of the transfer, with the annual confirmation serving as a mandatory year-end refresh to ensure the register mirrors the Register of Members.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% for Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax); the aggregate rate ranges across communes with varying local multipliers.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No tax holiday is available for an industrial quick-freezing operation. Permanent incentives: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends/capital gains (10% or EUR 1.2m ownership threshold and 12-month holding); 80% exemption for net qualifying IP income under the Luxembourg IP box; no Luxembourg withholding tax on cross-border interest/royalties.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (unlimited carry-forward for corporate income tax and municipal business tax; no carry-back permitted)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 541 (Déclaration d'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and Form 543 (impôt commercial communal), filed electronically with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via MyGuichet.lu/RTS; additional net wealth tax filing via Form 542.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one return per accounting year; quarterly advance payments of estimated CIT and municipal business tax are required)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally within 5 months after the accounting year-end (calendar-year company: 30 April/31 May of the following year); electronic filing benefits from an automatic extension to 30 June; further extensions to 31 December may be granted in writing by the tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter registered company name, legal form (SARL), RCS number / ELF code, tax number (RID), accounting year-end, activity code ISIC 1074 / NAICS 311412, and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company with a Luxembourg PE must enter the Luxembourg branch registration and local agent details; the foreign head-office address must be declared if they are the taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report accounting profit/loss from the frozen dim sum production and sale activity under Luxembourg GAAP before fiscal adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents should restrict this line to net profit objectively attributable to the Luxembourg PE under OECD PE profit-attribution rules, not world-wide income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back non-deductible expenses including excessive royalties, deemed director compensation, and statutory disallowances; subtract tax-exempt items such as participation dividends and the IP-box exempt portion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must apply arm's-length rules to intercompany management fees; deductions for payments to foreign entities without economic substance and without WHT documentation are disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Part III – Withholding tax credits and prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare foreign WHT recoverable and Luxembourg quarterly prepayments to compute the residual CIT/municipal business tax due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the tax residency certificate and underlying contract for foreign WHT credits; unused Luxembourg WHT credits are refundable to non-resident tax-neutral entities only when a PE exists and reporting conditions are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach director's report, balance sheet, tax schedules, participation exemption annexes, CbC-related slips if group turnover exceeds EUR 750m, and contemporaneous transfer pricing local file if thresholds are met.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents filing through a Luxembourg PE must include the PE's financial statements and the PE-related transfer pricing documentation; master file must be kept ready for the ACD within 60 days.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late submission triggers a 10% automatic tax surcharge on the reassessed tax, monthly late-payment interest at 0.6% (7.2% p.a.), and administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 in criminal cases; failure to maintain transfer pricing documentation may attract 60-day default record penalties and forfeiture of the burden of proof.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; 0% for qualifying Luxembourg/EU parent companies with at least 10% shareholding held for at least 12 months under the domestic participation exemption and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; DTA rates may reduce dividend WHT to 0-15% depending on ownership, residence, and beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must deliver a current tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by its state of residence and, where required, an ownership certificate to the paying Luxembourg SARL before distribution. The payer submits the prescribed relief-at-source application to the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration; if withholding is nevertheless applied, the recipient files a refund claim within the statutory limitation period (generally five years), attaching the TRC, board minutes approving the dividend, payment receipts, and DTA analysis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no domestic withholding tax on cross-border interest or royalties (0%); under DTAs and the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, qualifying related enterprises generally obtain 0% treaty withholding; royalty/interest income is taxable only if attributable to a Luxembourg PE.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR; mandatory OECD Local File/Master File is expected when the Luxembourg entity exceeds at least two of the 'large undertaking' thresholds (total assets > EUR 4,400,000; net turnover > EUR 8,800,000; average employees > 50) or when the multinational group must file CbC reports (consolidated revenue >= EUR 750,000,000); below these thresholds the ACD may still demand contemporaneous documentation within 60 days.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style ESR, but economic substance is decisive under ATAD, BEPS Action 5, tax abuse case law, and the participation exemption. A frozen-food operating SARL must maintain in-country premises, operative staff, inventory, decision-making board meetings, local bank accounts, logistics control, and real financial risk; a conduit arrangement will be disregarded for tax purposes and treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting sales from quick-frozen dim sum invoices; overstating procurement from shell suppliers; manipulating inventory shrinkage or cost records; deliberately disguising private expenses as factory costs in the Form 541 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty of up to 5 years' imprisonment and fines up to EUR 250,000 or up to half of the evaded tax; automatic 10% administrative surcharge; 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; full reassessment and loss of beneficial tax regimes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations become personally criminally liable and may be banned from managing Luxembourg companies; the corporate veil can be pierced where funds are diverted, enabling civil restitution, asset seizures, and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SARL owns the frozen food factory but has no Luxembourg management, no factory workforce, no substantive board minutes, all material functions in another state, and exists mainly to channel income and profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD disregards the artificial entity under ATAD/GAAR and abuse-of-law doctrine; profits are reallocated to the true economic owner, DTA and EU directive benefits are denied, plus 10% surcharge and 0.6% monthly late-payment interest; administrative fines for false documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly liable for tax debts where the shell structure is used to strip assets; Luxembourg courts can disqualify directors, impose civil restitution obligations, and issue travel bans during fraud investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The factory sells frozen dim sum to a related distributor below cost while paying group marketing and service fees at 12% of turnover without comparability analysis; no Local File/Master File produced within 60 days; no CUP/TNMM/benchmark documentation; no risk-functional adjustment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment to the arm's-length price; secondary recharacterization as hidden dividend/contribution; penalty of 10% on the excess tax and interest at 0.6% per month; failure to supply documentation reverses the taxpayer's evidentiary position and triggers daily fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers are personally accountable for maintaining contemporaneous TP documentation; if penalties force insolvency, directors may face creditor claims for wrongful management and travel bans during judicial examinations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / sanctions risk in trade finance and wire settlements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of Swift LC/TT payments without proper KYC/KYB policies; repetitive 30-day prepayments from shell purchasers; settlement to third-party accounts in high-risk jurisdictions; invoicing mismatch with physical goods for frozen food shipments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Luxembourg AML/CFT law, fines up to EUR 2.5 million for legal persons and imprisonment up to 5 years for individuals; obligatory disgorgement of proceeds; freezing of company bank accounts; removal from commercial registry and regulatory disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML duties cannot be fully delegated; directors are subject to personal fines and disqualification; investigating judges may impose asset freezes, passport surrender, and travel bans where asset flight is feared.
